what: Two rectangle screens drawn to break the conventions by a pixel or a few: Checkout with its footer 4.29px past the screen's bottom edge (the 2026-08-07 case), and Settings with a header band spanning 70% of its width, a 29px square, 19px text, a 7px-thin bar, two boxes side by side that overlap 40% vertically, two overlapping cards and 8px text.
why: Findings are listed in the order the lint gives them: depth first, each container's siblings before its children. The positive case for the geometry lint (ADR-002, SPEC-008 test case 1): one finding per rule the CLI can draw. The footer reproduces the failure that motivated PR 4: the reading says '1 screen could not be named' and the lint names the cause.
notes: Drawn 2026-11-17 on port 3072 with `apply` and exported with `excalidraw-canvas export`; not patched. No tab was open, so every size is the one given.
KI-6's oversized annotation needs a person's mark (origin human), which `apply` cannot make; it is tested inline in tests/wireframe-lint.test.mjs.
The footer, holding its own text, is promoted to a screen of its own, which no heading names: `ftr` is the unnamed screen in the score, read between Checkout and Settings, exactly as on 2026-08-07.
